judgement.why: This is the same photo-intake replay question already judged, and the relevant texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: The outcome of replaying an intake_id with conflicting photo content
quotes:
`PhotoValidationError` for a publication of another project or a section
outside it; `PhotoConflictError` for a replay that differs or belongs to
another project.
precedent.why: The public operation rejects reuse of intake_id with differing content or another project.

topics.topic: Product action that creates the first manual BudgetVersion
questions: How does a project acquire its one manual BudgetVersion before the first manual SectionPlan is written?
Which product action creates the first manual BudgetVersion for a project?
What product action creates a project's first manual BudgetVersion?

judgement.why: This is the same first-manual-BudgetVersion creation question already judged, and the relevant texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: When and by whom a project's manual BudgetVersion is created
quotes: `module:budget_management`. Return the project's one manual budget version, creating it empty when absent.

A18: at most one manual version per project; a new one is `inactive` and is
never activated implicitly; A13 (`budget.manual_version_create` only when it
is created).

A18 (stable
`PortalSection` identity; imported plans never change; a missing manual
version is created as `ensure_manual_budget` does)
precedent.why: The later API defines ensure_manual_budget and also makes the first manual-section upsert create a missing manual version.

quotes: `module:budget_management`. Make one budget version of the project the active one.

the

captured time in one transaction
precedent.why: The activation operation applies to the requested retained version and lists no terminal deactivated state, so a previously deactivated version can be requested again.

topics.topic: Whether a disabled ServicePrincipal can be reactivated
questions: Can a disabled ServicePrincipal be returned to active status?
Can a disabled ServicePrincipal be returned to active status?
Is `disabled` terminal, or may an administrator return a ServicePrincipal to `active`?

quotes:
- **Created/modified by:** administrator. `name`, `source_type` and
  `scope_mode` are set at creation and never change; the only modification
  is the status change `active ↔ disabled` (disabling revokes every
  credential of the principal). Grants of a `granted_projects` principal
  therefore never meet a scope switch.
`active → disabled` (Meaning).
judgement.why: The Meaning permits re-enabling while the Lifecycle candidate makes disabled terminal.

events: An administrator attempts to change that same ServicePrincipal back to active.

topics.topic: ProducerProjectGrant eligibility for disabled or all-projects principals
questions: May an administrator create a ProducerProjectGrant for a disabled principal or for an `all_projects` principal?
May an administrator create a ProducerProjectGrant for a disabled ServicePrincipal?
May an administrator create ProducerProjectGrant records for a principal whose scope mode is `all_projects`?

quotes:
### Errors

Access-management failures; `ScopedNotFoundError` for a project the Registry
does not know or an unknown principal; `ArchivedProjectRejected` for an
inactive project; `AuthorizationRejected` for an existing active grant;
`RegistryBoundaryError`.
judgement.why: The later operation's closed failures impose no active-principal or granted_projects-scope precondition, so grants may be created for disabled and all-projects principals.

precedent.topic: The ProjectOverview shape when Registry context is unavailable
quotes:
- `ProjectOverview` — the project context is absent when Registry cannot be
  read, and a `project_availability` says so, like the other five pairs; a
  Registry outage no longer fails the whole overview (Factory `d2c4511e`,
  2026-08-09).
precedent.why: The carried change explicitly defines the current shape and supersedes the former required project field.

quotes: - managed sessions with expiry, revocation, and sign-out-everywhere;
